com.wac.autocore.test

Class ErrorBoundaryProof

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.wac.autocore.test.ErrorBoundaryProof

  • public final class ErrorBoundaryProof
extends java.lang.Object
    A12: an invalid customer number is a rule violation with a message worth reading, and a database that stops answering is another kind of error. Neither a failed read nor a failed write may end as a quiet null. The proof goes through the service layer only, and builds its own database, so the real one is never touched and the proof runs on any machine. No arguments: the database is the proof's own, built from the schema files on the classpath.

      • NO_CUSTOMER

        private static final int[] NO_CUSTOMER
        Numbers that cannot be a customer: one that is simply not in the register, and the ones the model uses to mean "none at all". Every one of them is a rule violation, never a technical error, and none of them may leave a row behind.

      • report

        private static boolean report(GarageSystem garage)
        Numbers that cannot be a customer. All of them have to be refused the same way, and the ones the model reads as "none at all" are the interesting ones: a zero that slips through is written as a reference to nobody instead of being turned down.

      • readable

        private static boolean readable(java.lang.String message)
        A message that says something. After A3 a rule violation carries a key and A5 lets the ui translate it, so what is required here is a text to read or to translate — not words. The check is the same on both sides of that change, which is why it lives here.
